verificationRecords.command: npm run test:browser:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run test:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run typecheck; npm run visual:glyph-reconciliation-experiment
verificationRecords.notes: Forty-one Chromium checks, 38 focused compositor tests, all TypeScript projects, and 46 stable captures passed. Wide and phone endpoint evidence reports zero source-target center-anchor residual. Visual inspection confirms arbitrary vertical travel is gone; the known late typography overlap remains visible for the next handoff slices.

The first focused run correctly rejected a 40041-byte experiment controller against the frozen less-than-40000-byte ceiling. The bounded repair deleted two unused dataset diagnostics and retained the ceiling; no budget was raised.

verificationRecords.notes: Five convergence-policy tests, 38 focused compositor tests, all TypeScript projects, the font-ready wide DPR1 and phone DPR2 Chromium resize/reload matrix, and 46 stable captures pass. Fourteen dense endpoint frames each contain 21 immutable observations spanning source, material, and native sides. The frozen controller ceiling remains intact.

verificationRecords.command: npm run test:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run test:canonical-equation-renderer; npm run typecheck
verificationRecords.notes: Forty-two focused compositor tests, five convergence ratchets, and all TypeScript projects pass. Tests cover exact-style and bounded-transform compatibility, reverse-symmetric translation and scale metrics, the recorded typography mismatch shape, invalid bounds, and explicit native-checkpoint settlement for paint, style, clip, revision, axis, translation, or scale incompatibility. No notation, character, class, viewport, or operation dispatch was introduced.
The first candidate test used strict decimal equality for a computed 1.47-pixel residual and failed at 1.4699999999999989. The repair changed only the assertion to a 1e-12 numeric tolerance.

The visual script's intentionally reduced browser return type omitted renderer-only observation fields. The repair added an explicit boundary cast to the full runtime observation type; runtime evidence was already complete and the comparison never dereferences DOM elements.

verificationRecords.command: npm run test:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run test:canonical-equation-renderer; npm run typecheck; npm run visual:glyph-reconciliation-experiment
verificationRecords.notes: Forty-five focused tests, five convergence ratchets, all TypeScript projects, and 46 visual captures pass. Fourteen dense frames select target-style reverse FLIP with continuous law status. Maximum recorded pre-handoff residual is 1.627314 pixels wide and 1.150895 pixels phone. The 5000-evaluation pure microcheck completes in about 180 milliseconds against a two-second ceiling.

verificationRecords.command: npm run test:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run test:canonical-equation-renderer; npm run typecheck
verificationRecords.notes: Forty-eight focused tests, five convergence ratchets, and all TypeScript projects pass. The plan has total correlation-to-target coverage, frozen nested geometry, exact inverse metrics, identity-only checkpoint fallback, no element references, and explicit durable-artifact exclusion.

The first realization pass used 120872 core source bytes against the frozen 120000-byte ceiling. The repair deleted the superseded translation-only handoff API and its isolated tests, which had no production consumers; the ceiling was not raised and the core now uses 116485 bytes.

The first browser assertion compared target markup before normalizing playback to the tested 0.999 frame, so the expected ownership opacity update appeared as a mutation. The repair applies the existing scene frame first, then snapshots native markup around realization; no realization code changed.

verificationRecords.command: npm run test:real-katex-glyph-compositor; npm run test:browser:real-katex-glyph-compositor -- --grep target-style realization; npm run test:canonical-equation-renderer; npm run typecheck; npm run check:architecture
verificationRecords.notes: Forty-three focused tests, the wide and phone Chromium realization test, five convergence ratchets, all TypeScript projects, and architecture gates pass. Target-style visuals are idempotently reused, finite, exact-font styled, aria-hidden and inert, stripped of semantic and interactive attributes, and report zero native mutations. Native source and target markup is byte-equal around realization. Core source is 116485 bytes and the controller remains below 40000 bytes.

allowedWork: Experiment and production native-KaTeX scene observation, reconciliation, track sampling, generic style adaptation, ownership, and settlement.
Stable fraction and reader visual entrypoints plus deterministic tests.
One reader adapter and default-route migration only after the fraction checkpoint is explicitly approved.
Deletion or retirement of renderer code superseded by the migrated exemplar.
Governed semantic and LLM fixtures compiling into the canonical renderer contract without rendered authority.
Project-memory and Theseus records needed to close the architecture fork while preserving unrelated user work.
disallowedWork: No fraction, plus, radical, viewport, card, KaTeX-class, or operation-specific correction logic.
No new paint kind, atom lifecycle, semantic taxonomy, durable glyph IR, or operation-specific geometry scheduler.
No model-authored DOM, CSS, coordinates, keyframes, timing tables, target mathematics, geometry, computed style, or backend plans.
No global equation-family rollout before both mandatory human checkpoints.
No graph, diagram, code, table, curriculum, media, package-loading, portable-publication, or unrelated UI work.
No permanent query-selected second reader implementation.
goal: Resolve the equation-renderer fork by proving or rejecting one canonical native-KaTeX scene renderer, then after human approval migrate one gold reader card and remove its duplicate path.
commitCadence: Commit every independently reversible verified slice with exact path staging and its completed Theseus evidence.
stopConditions: Stop if a typography fix requires any plus, fraction, radical, viewport, KaTeX-class, card, expression, or operation exception.
Stop if the fraction endpoint jerk remains or a generic bound is exceeded at the slice-14 checkpoint.
Stop if a new paint kind, atom lifecycle, semantic taxonomy, durable glyph IR, or operation-specific scheduler is required.
Stop if moving paint gains accessibility, focus, annotation, Cloze, hover, interaction, or export authority.
Stop if native endpoint typography, mathematics, or semantic DOM must be mutated.
Stop if DOM, geometry, computed style, tracks, keyframes, or backend plans enter durable animation or LLM data.
Stop if a migrated exemplar cannot delete or disable its superseded renderer path.
Stop if ordinary reader routes exceed five percent regression or acquire unintended compositor code.
Stop if direct seek, rewind, reduced motion, static output, headless output, or production closure fails without one bounded generic repair.
Stop at slice 14 and slice 24 for explicit human approval; absent, rejected, or mixed approval forbids continuation.
Stop if work expands into deferred domains or cannot avoid unrelated dirty-worktree changes.

slices.title: renderer-inventory
slices.summary: Mapped the default reader material path, query-selected scene path, canonical scene-core candidate, active editor hosts, reference-only KaTeX transition code, and experimental evidence. Frozen retirement rules preserve every distinct capability and confirm the fraction gate can proceed without scope expansion.

slices.title: acceptance-and-complexity-ratchet
slices.summary: Added a typed convergence policy and stable focused test command. The ratchet fixes one current default reader, one temporary query scaffold with target zero, five paint kinds, six lifecycles, four core modules, source and payload ceilings, five-percent route regression, and forbidden special-case vocabulary. All focused, type, and architecture checks pass.

slices.title: same-baseline-fraction-fixture
slices.summary: Moved the generic review equation wrappers from separate 34/70-percent rows to one 50-percent center anchor. Wide and phone source/target centers now match at zero residual; 41 Chromium checks, 38 focused tests, typecheck, and 46 stable captures pass. The late typography overlap remains deliberately visible for the next generic handoff slices.

slices.title: dense-endpoint-style-telemetry
slices.summary: Added generic correlated handoff measurement spanning native source, material clone, and native target atoms. Dense 96-to-100-percent wide and phone evidence now validates every correlation's geometry, baseline or rule geometry, style/transform fingerprint, and wrapper context with deterministic font-ready resize/reload repetition. The first ceiling failure was repaired by deleting unused diagnostics, not relaxing the budget.

slices.title: generic-typography-handoff-law
slices.summary: Added a pure renderer-session handoff law over measured paint observations. It distinguishes exact-style compatibility, bounded typography transforms, and unsupported native-checkpoint settlement; exposes inverse translation/scale metrics; preserves the five-kind/six-lifecycle vocabulary; and uses no glyph identity or notation cases. Forty-two focused tests, the convergence ratchet, and typecheck pass.

slices.title: candidate-model-comparison
slices.summary: Compared target-style reverse FLIP, bounded dual-endpoint interpolation, and exact checkpoint settlement as immutable pure candidates. All fourteen recorded dense frames pass the generic law and select reverse FLIP because it combines exact target paint with geometry-only transit and zero native mutations. Added numeric decision evidence and a deterministic 5000-evaluation microcheck; focused, type, ratchet, and visual checks pass.

slices.title: selected-style-plan
slices.summary: Compiled target-style reverse FLIP into a frozen renderer-session style plan linked only to measured endpoint paint and existing scene correlations. Exact inverse geometry is stored for eligible entries; unsupported scenes receive identity transforms and native-checkpoint settlement. Total coverage, immutability, target-paint identity, and durable serialization exclusion pass 48 focused tests, ratchets, and typecheck.

slices.title: html-clone-realization
slices.summary: Applied the immutable target-style plan to ordinary HTML paint clones through one scene-level realization path. Wide and phone Chromium evidence proves finite geometry, exact target font paint, idempotent clone reuse, inert and aria-hidden ownership, stripped semantic/focus attributes, and untouched native endpoint DOM. Deleted the unused translation-only predecessor to bring core source from an initial 120872-byte failure down to 116485 without raising the ceiling.
